history.origins:
Country/Region of Origin: France. Tarot was introduced into France in the early 16th century; the dominant form now popular is the 19th-century rule set from Bourgogne-Franche-Comté. The game is played in France and French-speaking Canada.
Time Period: Early 16th century introduction; 19th-century revival with Tarot Nouveau
Historical Development: Evolved from Italian tarocchi; French-suited Tarot Nouveau supplanted Tarot de Marseille; Fédération Française de Tarot formed 1973; second-most popular card game in France after Belote.
Cultural Significance: Popular social and competitive game in France; also played in French-speaking Canada.
timeline: Modern Era: Continues to be played worldwide

rules.objective: Taker plays alone vs three defenders. Win enough card points: 56/51/41/36 depending on number of Oudlers (bouts: 21, 1, Excuse) in tricks.
rules.gameplay: 1. Deal: 6 to Dog, 18 each (4-player). 2. Bidding: Petite, Garde, Garde Sans, Garde Contre. 3. Taker takes Dog, discards 6. 4. Play 18 tricks; follow suit, trump if void. 5. Count points: bouts and Kings 4.5 each; Queens 3.5; Knights 2.5; Jacks 1.5; others 0.5.
keyRules: Follow suit; if void, play trump
Taker needs 56/51/41/36 points depending on Oudlers in tricks
Bouts (21, 1, Excuse) and Kings count 4.5 each
